title: Salt and Ember
premise: Hazel Pemberton, exiled for a storm she swears she never called, keeps the ledgers of the Vellum Guild, which trades in impossible things: bottled grief, borrowed years, names not yet earned. When the border wards collapse and the stars go dark, her homeland of Corvale is erased from every map and memory but hers — because Hazel's ledgers are written in storm-light, and storm-light remembers. To escape a country that officially no longer exists, she must trace the guild's oldest debt back to its origin: the Ember Court, which bought Corvale's sky and sold its name. The trail leads to her own family's inheritance — her mother signed the original contract — and to the truth that Hazel's exile was engineered to keep her from reading page one. In the end, Hazel calls the storm she was punished for, not as destruction but as testimony, forcing the Ember Court to honor a debt it cannot survive paying; Corvale is restored at the cost of Hazel's own recorded memories, and she walks out of the story a stranger who chose to forget herself so a nation could remember.
about_author: G. M. Delacroix is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloging trade ledgers from defunct merchant houses before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about paperwork, memory, and the violence hidden in fine print, and live somewhere with unreliable weather.

chapters.title: The Ledger Room
chapters.summary: Hazel Pemberton catalogs an impossible acquisition — a jar of someone else's childhood — in the Vellum Guild's cellar archives. Her POV establishes her precision, her exile, and her loneliness. Emotional beat: quiet competence masking grief.

chapters.title: Ink That Remembers
chapters.summary: A client tries to buy back a memory the Guild has already sold. Hazel refuses the refund; guild law forbids it. Her POV shows the cruelty of the system she serves. Beat: first crack in her loyalty.

chapters.title: The Night Without Stars
chapters.summary: The stars go out mid-audit. The border wards fall seconds later. Hazel watches Corvale vanish from the Guild's own maps while her ledger pages still glow. Her POV. Beat: terror and strange vindication.

chapters.title: Erased
chapters.summary: Guildmaster Oren Vey claims no country called Corvale ever existed — and no clerk named Pemberton either, yet he can't explain her presence. Hazel realizes her storm-light ink makes her un-erasable. Beat: isolation sharpened into purpose.

chapters.title: Debt of the House
chapters.summary: Digging into the oldest folio, Hazel finds her mother's signature on a contract dated before Hazel's birth: 'the sky of Corvale, in perpetuity.' Her POV. Beat: betrayal begins.

chapters.title: The Client Who Shouldn't Know
chapters.summary: A stranger named Ilex arrives asking for a door out of a country that doesn't exist — the exact phrase Hazel whispered alone. He knows too much. His POV reveals he's hunting the same contract. Beat: wary alliance.

chapters.title: Storm-Light Testimony
chapters.summary: Hazel demonstrates her ink's memory to Ilex: pages replay the night of her exile, and the storm she was convicted of calling appears — wrong. Someone else called it wearing her shape. Beat: rage rekindled.

chapters.title: The Ember Court
chapters.summary: Ilex explains the buyer behind the contract: the Ember Court, a parliament of fire that purchases skies, seasons, and sovereignty. Their POV chapter shows them noticing Hazel's glowing ledgers. Beat: the hunters become aware.

chapters.title: Sold Downriver
chapters.summary: Oren sells Hazel's location to the Court to save the Guild. She flees with one ledger and burns the rest deliberately — the memories inside scream. Her POV. Beat: guilt and resolve entwined.

chapters.title: The Road That Isn't There
chapters.summary: Traveling through terrain that keeps forgetting itself, Hazel and Ilex follow the contract's clause-path toward the Court. A village greets Hazel by name though it never met her — Corvale's residue. Beat: eerie hope.

chapters.title: What the River Owed
chapters.summary: They barter passage with a ferryman who accepts payment in forgotten things. Hazel pays with her memory of her mother's face. Ilex's POV shows him flinching — he recognizes something. Beat: cost made intimate.

chapters.title: Ash Parliament
chapters.summary: First sight of the Ember Court: a citadel built from burned treaties, where fire ministers debate in cinders. Hazel infiltrates as a records-clerk. Beat: dread dressed as confidence.

chapters.title: Page One
chapters.summary: Hazel reaches the original contract and reads the full terms: Corvale's sky traded for her mother's life — and a clause naming Hazel as collateral, exiled precisely so she'd never read this. Beat: devastation reframed as clarity.

chapters.title: The Shape-Wearer
chapters.summary: The impostor who called the exile-storm appears: Sable, the Court's enforcer, wearing stolen faces. Confrontation in the archive stacks. Hazel escapes barely alive. Beat: fear with teeth.

chapters.title: Ilex's Confession
chapters.summary: Ilex admits he was the Court's auditor sent to verify Corvale's erasure — until he read the ledgers and defected. His POV. Beat: trust rebuilt on broken ground.

chapters.title: The Guild's Last Entry
chapters.summary: Oren, ruined by his betrayal, sends Hazel the Guild's founding ledger: the Vellum Guild itself was created to keep debts honest when courts wouldn't. Beat: legacy and inheritance theme crystallized.

chapters.title: Clause and Counter-Clause
chapters.summary: Hazel finds a flaw: the contract requires the debtor's informed consent renewed each century. The renewal is due in nine days — at the Court's centennial sitting. Beat: a clock starts ticking.

chapters.title: Recruiting the Forgotten
chapters.summary: Hazel gathers others erased by Court contracts: a cartographer who mapped nowhere, a soldier whose war was unwritten. Ensemble chapter, rotating POVs. Beat: solidarity from ash.

chapters.title: Sable's Offer
chapters.summary: Sable offers Hazel her old life back — reinstated name, lifted exile — if she surrenders the ledgers. Hazel sees the offer is another forged signature. Beat: temptation refused.

chapters.title: The Ferryman's Price Again
chapters.summary: To reach the capital before the sitting, they need the ferryman once more. This time he asks for Hazel's memory of why she became a clerk. She pays. Beat: sacrifice compounding; she's forgetting her own motives.

chapters.title: Midnight Audit
chapters.summary: Inside the capital, Ilex uses his old credentials to open the Court's books. What he finds: thousands of countries, all purchased, all 'never existed.' His POV. Beat: scale of horror revealed.

chapters.title: The Fire Ministers
chapters.summary: The centennial sitting opens. Hazel, disguised, hears the ministers renew contracts by rote — consent manufactured through edited memory. Beat: cold fury.

chapters.title: Unmasked
chapters.summary: Sable exposes Hazel on the floor of the sitting. The Court moves to erase her on the spot — but her storm-light ink resists their fire. Beat: public defiance.

chapters.title: Testimony Interrupted
chapters.summary: Hazel attempts to read her ledger aloud as legal testimony. The ministers extinguish the chamber lights; without light, storm-ink goes silent. Beat: despair at the threshold of victory.

chapters.title: Ilex Burns Bright
chapters.summary: Ilex ignites himself — a former ember-minister's last trick — to give the chamber light long enough for Hazel to finish reading. His POV ends mid-sacrifice. Beat: devastating loyalty.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: By Ilex's dying flame, Hazel reads the whole contract into the record. The Court's own law binds it: the debt must be honored. The ministers panic. Beat: triumph shadowed by loss.

chapters.title: What Honoring Costs
chapters.summary: The fine print surfaces: restoring Corvale requires a memory of equal weight to a nation. The Court proposes Hazel's entire recorded past. Beat: impossible arithmetic.

chapters.title: Sable Unmasked Further
chapters.summary: Hazel learns Sable is a previous debtor — a person the Court hollowed into an enforcer, wearing stolen lives because she has none left. Beat: enemy becomes mirror.

chapters.title: The Storm She Never Called
chapters.summary: Flashback resolved: Sable called the exile-storm in Hazel's shape, on the Court's orders, to bury the contract's witness. Hazel forgives nothing but understands everything. Beat: justice clarified.

chapters.title: Negotiation in Cinders
chapters.summary: Hazel counters: she'll pay with her memories willingly — but only if the Court restores every erased country, not just Corvale. The ministers refuse; the debt-law forces reconsideration. Beat: audacity.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Map
chapters.summary: The forgotten allies act: the cartographer redraws the erased borders from memory, giving the debt a shape to fill. Rotating POVs. Beat: ordinary people doing extraordinary bookkeeping.

chapters.title: Renewal Refused
chapters.summary: At the moment of centennial renewal, Hazel — as inherited co-signatory — formally refuses consent on her mother's behalf. The contract begins collapsing. Beat: inheritance reclaimed as power.

chapters.title: Collapse
chapters.summary: The Court's citadel, built of voided treaties, starts burning from its foundations. Sable chooses to stay; Hazel drags her out anyway. Beat: mercy as rebellion.

chapters.title: The Calling
chapters.summary: Outside the falling citadel, Hazel finally calls the storm — the real one, hers — to carry the testimony of every erased nation into the sky being restored. Beat: climax; exile's punishment becomes her instrument.

chapters.title: Sky Returned
chapters.summary: Stars reignite over redrawn borders. Countries remember themselves. But the payment comes due: Hazel's ledgers blank page by page, taking her past with them. Beat: bittersweet ascension.

chapters.title: What Hazel Forgot
chapters.summary: Told partly from Sable's POV: Hazel, memory-stripped, doesn't recognize her own name. Sable, given Hazel's surrendered memories to hold, becomes her keeper. Beat: role reversal, tenderness.

chapters.title: The New Ledger
chapters.summary: Sable begins writing down who Hazel was, reading it to her nightly. Some entries make Hazel cry without knowing why. Beat: grief and gratitude braided.

chapters.title: Corvale Remembers Her
chapters.summary: Restored Corvale honors its witness with a monument — but Hazel, visiting, feels only a stranger's nostalgia. The country insists on remembering what she cannot. Beat: inheritance passed both ways.

chapters.title: Entry One
chapters.summary: Sable writes the final entry: not what Hazel lost, but what she chose. Hazel asks to hear it again. Beat: identity rebuilt from choice rather than memory.

chapters.title: Salt and Ember
chapters.summary: Hazel takes up a pen in a small guild office by the sea, keeping new ledgers in ordinary ink — and finds, faintly, storm-light rising where she writes. Some things are inherited deeper than memory. Final beat: quiet, earned beginning.
